Preview PWT and Production sheet columns and headers: $ python3 - <<'PY' import openpyxl wb=openpyxl.load_workbook('/root/test-supply.xlsx') ws=wb['PWT'] for r in range(1,6):     print(r,[ws.cell(r,c).value for c in range(1,6)]) print('max_row',ws.max_row,'max_col',ws.max_column) # show last header row for c in range(1,10):     v=ws.cell(1,c).value     if v is not None:         print('col',c,openpyxl.utils.get_column_letter(c),v)  ws2=wb['Production'] # show header row 5 cols C-N print('Production row5 C-N:', [ws2.cell(5,c).value for c in range(3,15)]) # show row36? table for production function maybe for r in range(30,60):     if any(ws2.cell(r,c).value is not None for c in range(1,12)):         vals=[ws2.cell(r,c).value for c in range(1,12)]         print(r,vals) PY

Check WEO_Data year coverage and existing formula slots: $ python3 - <<'PY' import openpyxl wb=openpyxl.load_workbook('/root/test-supply.xlsx', read_only=True) ws=wb['WEO_Data'] # find first 200 rows year values years=[] for r in range(8,200):     y=ws.cell(r,2).value     if isinstance(y,int):         years.append((r,y,ws.cell(r,3).value,ws.cell(r,4).value)) print('first years:', years[:10]) print('last in first200:', years[-1]) # find maximum row with a year in column B by scanning down until blank gap >1000 in chunks max_row=ws.max_row print('max_row',max_row) # sample some positions for r in [8,28,48,68,88,108,128,148,168,188]:     print(r, ws.cell(r,2).value) PY

Try fetching Georgia WEO real GDP and growth via IMF API: $ python3 - <<'PY' import requests, json base='https://www.imf.org/external/datamapper/api/v1/' for ind in ['NGDP_R','NGDP_RPCH']:     url=base+ind+'/GEO'     r=requests.get(url,timeout=30)     print(ind, r.status_code, r.headers.get('content-type'))     print(r.text[:200]) PY

Fetch IMF DataMapper JSON for NGDP_R and NGDP_RPCH: $ curl -s 'https://www.imf.org/external/datamapper/api/v1/NGDP_R/GEO' | head -c 300; echo; curl -s 'https://www.imf.org/external/datamapper/api/v1/NGDP_RPCH/GEO' | head -c 300; echo

Download IMF API JSON and parse GEO series with python json: $ python3 - <<'PY' import json,urllib.request  def fetch(url):     with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=60) as f:         return f.read().decode('utf-8')  for ind in ['NGDP_R','NGDP_RPCH']:     url=f'https://www.imf.org/external/datamapper/api/v1/{ind}/GEO'     txt=fetch(url)     data=json.loads(txt)     print(ind, data.keys())     # try extract values     vals=data.get('values',{}).get(ind,{}).get('GEO')     print('has GEO values?', vals is not None)     if vals:         years=sorted(vals.keys())         print('minyear',years[0],'maxyear',years[-1],'n',len(years))         print('sample', {y:vals[y] for y in years[-5:]}) PY

Inspect IMF API metadata for NGDP_R endpoint: $ python3 - <<'PY' import json,urllib.request url='https://www.imf.org/external/datamapper/api/v1/NGDP_R' with urllib.request.urlopen(url,timeout=60) as f:     data=json.load(f) print(data.keys()) print('api:', data.get('api')) print('has values', 'values' in data) PY

Test IMF API NGDP_R for USA to see if values exist: $ python3 - <<'PY' import json,urllib.request for c in ['USA','GEO','SDN']:     url=f'https://www.imf.org/external/datamapper/api/v1/NGDP_R/{c}'     with urllib.request.urlopen(url,timeout=60) as f:         data=json.load(f)     vals=data.get('values',{}).get('NGDP_R',{}).get(c)     print(c,'has values',bool(vals), 'keys', list(data.keys())[:3]) PY

Download PWT 11.0 Excel from Dataverse API: $ mkdir -p /root/data && curl -L -o /root/data/pwt11.xlsx 'https://dataverse.nl/api/access/datafile/554105' && ls -lh /root/data/pwt11.xlsx

Inspect PWT 11 Excel for sheet names and Georgia data columns: $ python3 - <<'PY' import openpyxl wb=openpyxl.load_workbook('/root/data/pwt11.xlsx', read_only=True) print(wb.sheetnames) ws=wb[wb.sheetnames[0]] print('first sheet dims', ws.max_row, ws.max_column) # find header row 1 values for first 20 columns hdr=[ws.cell(1,c).value for c in range(1,51)] print('hdr sample', hdr[:20]) # locate columns for countrycode, year, rnna, rkna for target in ['countrycode','country','year','rnna','rkna']:     if target in hdr:         print(target,'col',hdr.index(target)+1) # find rows for GEO 2023 by scanning cc_col=hdr.index('countrycode')+1 year_col=hdr.index('year')+1 rnna_col=hdr.index('rnna')+1 rkna_col=hdr.index('rkna')+1 rows=[] for r in range(2, ws.max_row+1):     if ws.cell(r,cc_col).value=='GEO':         y=ws.cell(r,year_col).value         if y in (1990,2000,2023):             rows.append((r,y,ws.cell(r,rnna_col).value,ws.cell(r,rkna_col).value))         if y==2023 and len(rows)>10:             break print('sample GEO rows', rows[:10]) PY

Parse PWT 11.0 Data sheet for Georgia rnna and rkna: $ python3 - <<'PY' import openpyxl wb=openpyxl.load_workbook('/root/data/pwt11.xlsx', read_only=True) ws=wb['Data'] hdr=[ws.cell(1,c).value for c in range(1,151)] for target in ['countrycode','country','year','rnna','rkna']:     print(target, 'col', hdr.index(target)+1) cc_col=hdr.index('countrycode')+1 year_col=hdr.index('year')+1 rnna_col=hdr.index('rnna')+1 rkna_col=hdr.index('rkna')+1 out=[] for r in range(2, ws.max_row+1):     if ws.cell(r,cc_col).value=='GEO':         y=ws.cell(r,year_col).value         out.append((y, ws.cell(r,rnna_col).value, ws.cell(r,rkna_col).value)) print('GEO years', out[0][0], out[-1][0], 'count', len(out)) print('sample', out[:3], out[-3:]) PY

Parse PWT Georgia rows efficiently with streaming: $ python3 - <<'PY' import openpyxl wb=openpyxl.load_workbook('/root/data/pwt11.xlsx', read_only=True) ws=wb['Data'] hdr=[c.value for c in next(ws.iter_rows(min_row=1,max_row=1))] cc_col=hdr.index('countrycode') year_col=hdr.index('year') rnna_col=hdr.index('rnna') rkna_col=hdr.index('rkna') out=[] for row in ws.iter_rows(min_row=2, values_only=True):     if row[cc_col]=='GEO':         out.append((row[year_col], row[rnna_col], row[rkna_col])) print('count',len(out),'years',out[0][0],out[-1][0]) print('last5', out[-5:]) PY

Parse PWT 11.0 using iter_rows values_only for Georgia: $ python3 - <<'PY' import openpyxl wb=openpyxl.load_workbook('/root/data/pwt11.xlsx', read_only=True, data_only=True) ws=wb['Data'] # header hdr=next(ws.iter_rows(min_row=1,max_row=1,values_only=True)) cc_i=hdr.index('countrycode') y_i=hdr.index('year') rnna_i=hdr.index('rnna') rkna_i=hdr.index('rkna') out=[] for row in ws.iter_rows(min_row=2, values_only=True):     if row[cc_i]=='GEO':         out.append((int(row[y_i]), row[rnna_i], row[rkna_i])) print('rows',len(out)) print(out[:3]) print(out[-3:]) PY
